summary.td1: Compares the value with the cases, in order.
summary.td2: Rendered when the value is === 'a'.
summary.td3: One block for several values.
summary.td4: Rendered when no case matches, wherever it is written.

elementRefs.title: Element refs
elementRefs.lead: #name on an element is an element ref, or ref: it names the element in the template, and the expressions read it, typed with the type of the element, an HTMLInputElement for an <input> or the class of a component. Event handlers call its methods, or pass it to the methods of the component. Not to be confused with the template variables, declared with @let.

naming.title: Naming an element
naming.example1: A field focused, cleared and read through its ref
naming.p1: The buttons come before the field and still use it: a handler runs once the template is rendered, when every element of its scope exists. field.focus() calls a method of the element, clear(field) passes the element to a method of the component, search(field.value) one of its properties.
naming.p2: Reading a property through a ref is not reactive: { field.value } shows the value the field had when the text was rendered. Follow the changes with an event, as the field does with (input), and keep them in a signal.
naming.p3: The class reaches an element ref too, without a selector: @Query.ref('field') holds the element named #field, and @Query.ref.all the ones of every row of an @for. See View queries.

types.title: The type of a ref
types.p1: A ref has the type of its element: the one the DOM declares for its tag, such as HTMLDialogElement for a <dialog> or SVGCircleElement for a <circle> inside an <svg>, or the class of a component, instantiated with its type arguments when it is generic. TypeScript checks every member read or called through it.
types.example1: A native dialog opened and closed by its methods
types.p2: The ref of a component is its instance, since the component is the element: its methods and its signals can be called too, as counter.reset() and { counter.count() } do in the first snippet.

scope.title: Scope and order
scope.p1: A ref is visible in the whole of its scope, inside other elements and before its own element too. A scope is the template, a branch of @if, a case of @switch, a row of @for, or the content of an element a structural directive is applied to: a ref declared there is not visible outside, and a nested scope can declare a ref named like an outer one, which it hides.
scope.p2: An element is created when the render reaches it, though. An event handler can use a ref declared after it, while any other expression, an interpolation, a binding or a condition, only reads the ones declared before: the compiler rejects the others.
scope.p3: Each row of the @for has its own note. Reversing the list moves the rows together with their fields, and with what you typed in them.
scope.p4: The compiler reports the refs used where they cannot be:

callout1.heading: Elements that may not exist
callout1.body: An element a structural directive is applied to, directly or by a conditional binding, cannot declare a ref, since the directive may not render it. Declare it on an element inside it, whose content is a scope of its own, or use an @if.

callout2.heading: Events during the render
callout2.body: A handler running while the template is still being rendered, for an event a child component emits from its onInit, may read a ref whose element is not created yet: it throws a ReferenceError naming the ref, instead of reading another one named like it.

callout3.heading: The track expression of @for
callout3.body: The track expression of a @for reads only the item and the implicit variables of the loop: it cannot read an element ref.

callout4.heading: Where a ref is declared
callout4.body: A ref is declared directly on the element, without a value, at most one per element: not inside a conditional binding, nor inside the parentheses of a directive. root, $event and the names starting with __ or $$ are reserved.

summary.title: Summary
summary.td1: Names the element, typed with the DOM interface of its tag, or with the class of its component.
summary.td2: Calls a method of the element, or of the component.
summary.td3: Passes the element, or one of its properties, to a method of the component.
summary.td4: Reads the element after its declaration: a property of the DOM is not a signal, so the text does not follow its changes.

let.title: @let
let.lead: @let name = value;, also called a template variable, names a part of a signal that the template reads several times, such as a field of the object it holds: @let address = user().address;, then address().city, instead of a getter in the class that only shortens the access. Computations stay in the class, in a computed or a method.

declaring.title: Declaring a @let
declaring.p1: A @let goes wherever content goes: its name, =, an expression and a ;, which is required. The value can span several lines, and a ; inside a string or between parentheses, brackets or braces does not end it. A @let renders nothing and cannot be assigned: its value follows the expression it is declared with.
declaring.p2: address reads user, so it is a signal: move() changes the user and updates the lines reading it. country reads a constant member, so it is a value, computed once.

signals.title: Signal or value
signals.p1: The compiler tells them apart by what the value reads, as it does for the bindings: a signal member, a method or a getter of the component reading one, a signal imported with @import, a variable of @for, a parameter of a template, or another @let that is a signal. Then the @let is a signal too, read with name(): it computes its value when it is read, and again when what it reads changes, so only the nodes reading it are updated. Otherwise it is a value, computed once when its scope is created, and read as name.
signals.p2: Its type is the one TypeScript infers for its value, a Computed of it for a signal. TypeScript reports a signal read without parentheses, as total.toFixed(2), and a value called as a function. A value written as a literal keeps its literal type: @let mode = 'grid'; is typed 'grid'.

scope.title: Scope and order
scope.p1: A @let has the scope of an element ref: the whole of the template, of a branch of @if, of a case of @switch, of a row of @for, of the content of a template or of an element a structural directive is applied to, inside other elements too. A nested scope can declare a @let named like an outer one, which it hides.
scope.p2: Each row has its own stats, a signal since it reads the item of the row: completing a task updates only the row of that member.
scope.p3: A @let is initialized when the render reaches it: an event handler can read it anywhere in its scope, while any other expression, its own value included, only reads it after its ;. The content of a template reads it only if every @render of the template comes after it. The compiler reports the others:

callout1.heading: Signals the compiler cannot follow
callout1.body: A function of another module, or a member of another object, reading a signal does not make a @let a signal: the compiler follows the members of the component, the imports and the variables of the template only. Such a @let is computed once: read the signal directly, or through a member of the component.

callout2.heading: Events during the render
callout2.body: A handler running while the template is still being rendered, for an event a child component emits from its onInit, may read a @let the render has not reached yet: it throws a ReferenceError naming it, instead of reading another one named like it.

callout3.heading: The track expression of @for
callout3.body: The track expression of a @for reads only the item and the implicit variables of the loop: it cannot read a @let, not even one declared outside of the loop.

callout4.heading: Where a @let is declared
callout4.body: A @let is declared among the content, never among the bindings of a tag, with a name of its own in its scope: TypeScript reports an element ref, a template or another @let named like it there. root, $event and the names starting with __ or $$ are reserved.

summary.title: Summary
summary.td1: Names the value of the expression in its scope: the expressions read it after its ;, the event handlers anywhere.
summary.td2: Reads a @let whose value reads a signal: it is a signal, updated when what it reads changes.
summary.td3: Reads a @let whose value reads no signal: a value, computed once.

reusableTemplates.title: Reusable templates with @render
reusableTemplates.lead: <template name(…)> declares a piece of template once, with typed parameters, like a function. @render name(…) renders it wherever content can go, and TypeScript checks the arguments as it checks the ones of a call.

declaring.title: Declaring and rendering
declaring.p1: A <template> is a declaration: it renders nothing where it is written. Its name follows the tag name, then its parameters, each with its type, between parentheses that are written also when there are none. Each @render renders a new instance of its content, with elements of its own.
declaring.p2: In the content, a parameter is a signal, read like the item of a @for: label(). When an argument changes, the instance is not rendered again: only the nodes reading the parameter are updated, as the amounts do when you press the button.

parameters.title: Parameters and their types
parameters.p1: A parameter takes any TypeScript type, also one the template imports with @import. The arguments of a @render are checked against the parameters, their number and the type of each one, and an argument is any expression of the template.
parameters.example1: A row template, typed with an imported type, rendered by a @for
parameters.p2: The template comes after the @for rendering it: a template is visible in the whole of its scope, before its declaration too. When the rows move, their instances move with them, and receive their new position in place.

optionalParameters.title: Optional parameters and default values
optionalParameters.p1: A parameter can be optional, note?: string, or have a default value, with its type or typed by the value: dense: boolean = false, label = item().name. A @render can then leave out its argument, and only the last parameters can be so.
optionalParameters.example1: Badges with a default tone and an optional count
optionalParameters.p2: The default value is used only when the argument is left out: an argument passed as undefined stays undefined, and TypeScript accepts it only if the type of the parameter does. Like in JavaScript, the default value reads what the content reads and the parameters before it, as signals, and it is a signal too: it updates when what it reads changes. An optional parameter left out holds undefined.

scope.title: What a template reads
scope.p1: The content of a template reads the names of the place it is declared in, like a closure: the members of the component, the imports, the element refs and the templates of its scope, the item of the @for around the declaration. It doesn't read the names of the place it is rendered in: pass them as arguments.
scope.p2: A template can render itself. The recursion ends where the data do, with an @if or a @for on the children, and every level is a new instance.
scope.example1: A tree rendered by a recursive template
scope.p3: The compiler reports the templates declared or rendered where they cannot be:

callout1.heading: SVG and MathML
callout1.body: The content of a template is created in the namespace of its declaration: a template declared among HTML elements renders HTML elements, one declared inside an <svg> renders SVG elements. Rendering it in another namespace is an error.

callout2.heading: Element refs read by a template
callout2.body: The content of a template is rendered where a @render is: an element ref of an enclosing scope that the content reads, outside of an event handler, must be declared before every @render of the template.

callout3.heading: Arguments and parameters
callout3.body: There are no rest parameters or destructuring, and an argument cannot be spread. A parameter after an optional one, or after one with a default value, must be so too.

callout4.heading: Where a template is rendered
callout4.body: A template is rendered by the template declaring it, in its scope: it cannot be passed to another component, nor read by the class.

summary.td2: Renders an instance of the template where it is written, checking the arguments against the parameters.
summary.td3: Reads a parameter in the content: a signal, updated when its argument changes.
summary.td4: An optional parameter, and parameters with a default value, typed as declared or by the value: a @render may leave out their arguments.

textInterpolation.title: Text interpolation
textInterpolation.lead: An expression in braces, in the middle of the text, becomes a text node showing its value. The compiler wires that node to the signals the expression reads: when one of them changes, the expression runs again and only that node is updated.

interpolatingValues.title: Interpolating values
interpolatingValues.example1: Six interpolations of the same state
interpolatingValues.p1: Each line updates by itself when you press a button, the one calling a method included: in text, the compiler wraps the whole expression in an effect, so whatever it reads, directly or through a method, is tracked. Attributes follow a stricter rule, explained in Binding.
interpolatingValues.p2: The expression is checked against the class of the component, like TypeScript code written outside of it: it can read the public members by name, without this, and the globals such as Math or JSON. What an expression may contain is listed in Expression syntax.

whatAValueBecomes.title: What a value becomes
whatAValueBecomes.p1: The value is converted to a string, with two exceptions: null and undefined become empty text.
whatAValueBecomes.p2: The last row is the most common mistake: a signal is a function, and without the call the text shows the function itself. Nothing reports it, since showing a function is valid.

build.title: Build and Vite plugin
build.lead: Templates and styles are compiled ahead of time by xaendarPlugin(), from @xaendar/build-tools. The CLI adds it to Vite on its own; a project driving Vite directly adds it to its configuration, after the transform of the decorators.

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.p1: The order matters. Babel compiles the standard decorators first, and the plugin then works on its output: it looks for the static blocks Babel generates in each decorated class, and adds its own registration before them. With the plugins in the wrong order, every component fails with the message shown in Installation.
configuration.p2: The plugin takes one option, customElements: the patterns of the tags of the custom elements of other libraries, such as ['sl-*'], which templates use like native elements, without importing them. The CLI passes the list declared in xaendar.json. See XaendarPluginOptions and Selectors and registration. It reads tsconfig.json from the folder Vite is started from, and uses its compiler options, including the strict ones, to type-check the templates.

whatThePluginDoes.title: What the plugin does
whatThePluginDoes.p1: Only files whose name ends with .xd.component.ts are compiled. For each component class in such a file, the plugin reads the options of @WebComponent, validates and claims the selector, type-checks the template against the class, and adds to the module two imports from virtual modules: the render function of the template and the stylesheet.
whatThePluginDoes.p2: Each template becomes a module exporting its render function. The signals parameter in its id lists the members of the class recognized as signals, which decide which bindings are reactive. Each stylesheet becomes a module exporting a CSSStyleSheet: components pointing to the same file share the same sheet.
whatThePluginDoes.p3: A .scss or .sass file is first compiled with the sass package, a .less file with less: optional peer dependencies of @xaendar/build-tools, which the project installs itself (see Styling). Comments are then removed from the CSS. In vite build, the CSS is also minified with Lightning CSS, unless the Vite configuration turns CSS minification off.

errors.title: Errors
errors.p1: Errors in a template are printed by the dev server and by the build, with the position in the template and the excerpt involved. They fail the build. In the dev server, the component they belong to is left without its render function, and throws when it is connected. The Error encyclopedia lists the messages.
errors.p2: Vite only strips the types of TypeScript. The plugin checks them: once the build ends, it type-checks the whole project as tsc --noEmit does, and fails if it finds errors. The dev server checks each file as it serves it: a file with type errors is not served, and its errors show in the terminal and in the Vite overlay.

devServer.title: Dev server
devServer.p1: The plugin watches, for each component, its template, its stylesheet and the files the stylesheet imports with Sass or Less, the classes it extends and the components its template imports. Editing any of them recompiles what depends on it, and the page reloads.

callout4.heading: The working directory matters
callout4.body: tsconfig.json is read from the folder Vite is started from, not from the folder of vite.config.ts. Start xd or Vite from the root of the project.

callout5.heading: CSS imports
callout5.body: @import rules in a .css file are dropped by the browser, since constructed stylesheets do not support them. The imports of Sass and Less work, because they are resolved at build time. See Styling.

cli.title: CLI
cli.lead: xd, from @xaendar/cli, creates projects and components, and runs Vite with the plugins Xaendar needs. There is nothing more to it: vite.config.ts stays a plain Vite configuration.

xdNew.title: xd new
xdNew.p1: The name of the project is used for the folder, for package.json, and for the root component, <name>-root. The generated files are described in Installation. The command stops if the folder exists and is not empty.
xdNew.p2: Unless --style gives it, the command asks the format of the stylesheets: css, scss, sass (the indented syntax) or less. An invalid --style stops the command before anything is written.
xdNew.p3: The answer is the number or the name of a format; an empty answer picks CSS, and an invalid one asks again. Without an interactive terminal, as in CI, the command uses CSS without asking. The format is the extension of the global stylesheet, src/styles.css or src/styles.scss for example, and of the stylesheets of the components; with SCSS, Sass or Less, package.json also gets sass or less among its devDependencies. xaendar.json records the settings of the project: the format, read by xd generate component, and, in customElements, the tags of other libraries used by the templates (see Selectors and registration).

xdStartAndXd.title: xd start and xd build
xdStartAndXd.p1: xd start (or xd s) runs the Vite dev server, xd build (or xd b) a production build. Both read vite.config.ts from the current folder and add two plugins to it: Babel, to compile the decorators, and the Xaendar plugin, to compile templates and styles. The details are in Build and Vite plugin. Everything else, such as the port, the root folder or the output folder, comes from the Vite configuration.

xdTest.title: xd test
xdTest.p1: xd test (or xd t) runs Vitest with the same plugins, in the DOM environment of happy-dom, and installs the global Signal before the specs, as main.ts does. The spec generated with each component adds its tag to the document and checks that it renders its template. Vitest watches the files, and runs them once in CI.

xdComponent.title: xd generate component
xdComponent.p1: The command creates a folder named after the component, with the class, the template, the stylesheet and a spec. The name is used as the selector, so it must be a valid custom element name; the class is named after it in PascalCase. The stylesheet has the format of the project: the command reads it from the nearest xaendar.json, looking from the target folder (--path or the current one) up, and writes user-card.xd.component.scss for scss, with a styleUrl pointing to it. Without xaendar.json, or without the format in it, the stylesheet is a .css file; a format the CLI does not know stops the command.
xdComponent.p2: Remember to import the new component in the templates using it, with @import: that also defines it.

callout2.heading: Invalid names
callout2.p1: Component names are checked before anything is written.
callout2.p2: The name of a project is checked too, before anything is written: it names the root component, <name>-root.

callout5.heading: The published packages are older than this documentation
callout5.p1: The packages published on npm as 0.12.0 predate the API described in this site: their @xaendar/core exports BaseWebComponent instead of CustomElement. A project created by a CLI built from the repository installs them, and its build fails. Until the next release, work inside the repository, as this site does.

languageService.title: Language service and VS Code
languageService.lead: The repository contains a VS Code extension for templates, made of two parts: a grammar for syntax highlighting, and a client starting @xaendar/language-server, meant to bring the checks of the compiler into the editor. Both are at an early stage: this page describes what they do today.

callout1.heading: Work in progress
callout1.body: The repository has no packaging step for the Marketplace, and the language server does not report diagnostics or offer completions yet. The compiler messages are available in the terminal of xd start, as described in Build and Vite plugin.

runningTheExtension.title: Running the extension
runningTheExtension.p1: The extension is built from the repository and started in a development window of VS Code.
runningTheExtension.p2: It activates in workspaces containing .xd.component.html files, associates them with the language Xaendar Template, and starts the server over IPC.

syntaxHighlighting.title: Syntax highlighting
syntaxHighlighting.p1: The grammar is injected into the HTML grammar of VS Code: templates keep the highlighting of HTML, and some Xaendar constructs get their own colors.

theLanguageServer.title: The language server
theLanguageServer.p1: The server is designed to compile each template as it is edited, with the same type-check shim used by the Vite plugin, and to turn the result into editor features:
theLanguageServer.li1: Diagnostics: after 300 ms without typing, the semantic errors of TypeScript on the template, at their position; syntax errors of the template at its first line.
theLanguageServer.li2: Completions: the completions of TypeScript inside template expressions, triggered by ., { and (.

callout1.heading: No template is ever associated with a component
callout1.body: To compile a template, the server must know the component class using it. The index mapping templates to components is built at startup, but the code filling it is disabled: every template is skipped, so neither diagnostics nor completions are produced.

callout2.heading: Interpolations are not highlighted
callout2.body: The grammar expects {{ expr }}, a syntax that Xaendar does not use. Interpolations written as { expr } in text, and directives, keep the colors of plain HTML.

callout3.heading: Other limits
callout3.body: The server announces hover support but implements no hover, and starts five seconds after the extension.

tutorial.title: Tutorial: a todo app
tutorial.lead: Build a small todo application in five steps. Each step adds one concept, and each example is the complete, working code of that step: compare the files of two consecutive steps to see exactly what changed.

step1AStatic.title: Step 1 — A static component
step1AStatic.p1: Every component starts as a class decorated with @WebComponent, pointing at its template and its stylesheet. The template is plain HTML for now.

step2StateIn.title: Step 2 — State in a signal
step2StateIn.p1: The todos move into a signal. The template renders them with @for, and shows their number with an interpolation. track todo().id tells @for how to recognise a todo across changes, so that its DOM can be reused.

step3AddingTodos.title: Step 3 — Adding todos
step3AddingTodos.p1: The (submit) listener calls add($event), which reads the form, appends a todo and resets the form. The update produces a new array: signals compare values by identity, so pushing into the existing array would notify nobody.

step4CompletingAnd.title: Step 4 — Completing and removing
step4CompletingAnd.p1: Each row gets a checkbox and a remove button. A conditional binding, @if (todo.done) { checked } written inside the tag, adds the checked attribute only to the done todos. A computed signal counts the remaining todos, and @if shows a message when the list is empty.

step5AChild.title: Step 5 — A child component and a filter
step5AChild.p1: The row moves into its own component, ex-todo-item. It receives the todo through a required input and reports what happens through two outputs, doneChange and removed. The parent keeps the state and adds a filter: a signal, a computed list of the visible todos, and a @switch for the footer.

whereToGoFrom.title: Where to go from here
whereToGoFrom.p1: The guides cover each concept in depth, with their edge cases: start from signals, inputs and lists.

[Lexer] Unknown flow-control keyword.cause: An @ in text starts a block: a keyword written without a space before its parenthesis (@if(…)), a keyword that does not exist (@unless, @empty), or a plain @, as in an email address.
[Lexer] Unknown flow-control keyword.fix: Write a space after the keyword, and &commat; or an interpolation such as { '@' } for a literal @.

[Lexer] Comment never closed: '<!--' wit.cause: An HTML comment opened with <!-- and never closed.

[Lexer] Unexpected character 'p' after '.cause: A literal < in text, as in 1 < 2, is read as the start of a tag.

[Lexer] Attribute value must start with.cause: An attribute value in single quotes, or without quotes.
[Lexer] Attribute value must start with.fix: Use double quotes for every attribute value.

[Lexer] Event must be included in Double.cause: A listener with more than one statement, such as (click)="save(); close()".
[Lexer] Event must be included in Double.fix: Call a single method, and do the rest in the method.

[Lexer] Event handler cannot be empty.cause: An arrow function as listener, such as (click)="() => go()".

[Lexer] No spaces are allowed in event h.cause: An assignment as listener, such as (click)="open = true".
[Lexer] No spaces are allowed in event h.fix: Move the assignment into a method.

[Lexer] Expected { after @import.fix: Use a named import: @import { Card } from …

[Lexer] Directives cannot be declared in.cause: A directive written inside the parentheses of another one.
[Lexer] Directives cannot be declared in.fix: Write the directives one after the other on the tag.

[Lexer] The properties of a structural d.cause: An @if or @switch inside the parentheses of a structural directive.
[Lexer] The properties of a structural d.fix: Apply the whole directive inside the condition, once per branch.

[Lexer] Structural directives cannot lis.cause: A listener inside the parentheses of a structural directive.
[Lexer] Structural directives cannot lis.fix: Write the listener on the tag, outside the directive.

[Parser] Expected closing tag input whil.cause: An element never closed: a void element without />, or a string or template literal never closed in an interpolation.
[Parser] Expected closing tag input whil.fix: Self-close void elements (<input />), and close every string and template literal.

[Parser] Expected closing tag div, found.cause: A closing tag written with a different case.
[Parser] Expected closing tag div, found.fix: Write opening and closing tags the same way.

[Parser] No transition function for toke.fix: Put the @else right after the closing brace of the @if.

[Parser] Attribute \"title\" is bound mo.cause: The same attribute written both outside and inside a conditional binding.
[Parser] Attribute \"title\" is bound mo.fix: Bind it only inside the condition, in every branch that needs it.

[Parser] Class \"on\" is bound more than.cause: The same [class.name] written twice on an element, or both outside and inside a conditional binding.
[Parser] Class \"on\" is bound more than.fix: Toggle it once, combining the conditions in its expression, or in every branch of one condition.

[Parser] [class.on] toggles the class by.cause: A class binding with a static value, or without a value.
[Parser] [class.on] toggles the class by.fix: Bind it to an expression in braces: [class.on]="{ active() }".

[Parser] \"[style.color]\" is not a bind.cause: An attribute name in brackets other than [class.name]: brackets only toggle classes.
[Parser] \"[style.color]\" is not a bind.fix: Bind the attribute without brackets, e.g. style="{ … }", or toggle a class with [class.name].

[Parser] [class.on] cannot be bound insi.cause: A class binding in the parentheses of a directive, or in a conditional binding inside them, which only bind the properties of the directive.
[Parser] [class.on] cannot be bound insi.fix: Move it among the bindings of the element.

[Parser] Directive \"exTint\" is applied.cause: The same directive applied twice to one element.
[Parser] Directive \"exTint\" is applied.fix: Apply it once; switch its inputs with a condition if needed.

[Parser] 'user(); as u' must be a single.cause: More than one expression where one is expected, as in @if (x; as y) or a; b.
[Parser] 'user(); as u' must be a single.fix: Write a single expression; read the value again inside the block.

[Parser] 'FirstAssignment' is not allowe.cause: A construct forbidden in expressions. The same message names the others: 'new', function expressions, 'ThisKeyword', 'AsExpression', 'RegularExpressionLiteral', 'CommaToken'.
[Parser] 'FirstAssignment' is not allowe.fix: Move the logic into a method or a computed signal of the class.

[Parser] 'let i' is not a valid alias id.cause: An alias of @for written with let.

[TypeChecker] foreign-thing selector is.cause: A tag with a dash that is neither a Xaendar component imported by the template nor declared in customElements: a missing @import, or a custom element of another library.
[TypeChecker] foreign-thing selector is.fix: Import the component; declare the tags of other libraries in the customElements of xaendar.json.

[TypeChecker] sl-button is both imported.cause: A tag that is a component imported by the template and also matches a pattern of customElements.
[TypeChecker] sl-button is both imported.fix: Narrow the pattern to the tags of the other library, or rename the selector of the component.

[TypeChecker] @@exTint selector is not a.fix: Import the directive class in the template.

[TypeChecker] Required property \"name\".cause: A required input bound only in some branches.
[TypeChecker] Required property \"name\".fix: Add an @else or @default branch binding it, or bind it outside the condition.

Property 'valuechange' does not exist on.cause: A listener for an event that is neither an output of the component nor a native event of its element: a different case, or a misspelled name.
Property 'valuechange' does not exist on.fix: Match the name of the accessor, letter by letter.

[TypeChecker] Unknown property \"shade\".cause: An input the directive does not declare.
[TypeChecker] Unknown property \"shade\".fix: Use the name of a @Property of the directive.

Property 'bubbly' does not exist on type.cause: A listener for an unknown event on a native element.
Property 'bubbly' does not exist on type.fix: Listen to custom events on the component emitting them, or on a component re-emitting them.

Type 'string' does not satisfy the expec.cause: A static value, always a string, bound to an input of another type.

Property 'secret' is private and only ac.cause: A private or protected member read by the template.

Property 'LIMIT' does not exist on type.cause: A module constant read by the template without importing it: the expressions read the members of the class and the names the template imports.
Property 'LIMIT' does not exist on type.fix: Import it in the template: @import { LIMIT } from './limits.ts'.

This comparison appears to be unintentio.cause: A readonly member initialized with a literal has a literal type, and the template is checked with it.
This comparison appears to be unintentio.fix: Annotate the member with a wider type.

Argument of type 'Set<number>' is not as.cause: @for over something that is neither an array nor a number: a Set, a Map, a string.
Argument of type 'Set<number>' is not as.fix: Convert it to an array, for instance in a computed signal.

Property '$count' does not exist on type.cause: $count is not one of the variables of @for.
Property '$count' does not exist on type.fix: Read the length of the list.

Cannot find name 'first'..cause: A member of the component as the value of an @case, which only accepts literals.

'root.prices.coffee' is possibly 'undefi.cause: The strict options of tsconfig.json, such as noUncheckedIndexedAccess, apply to templates too.
'root.prices.coffee' is possibly 'undefi.fix: Use ?. or ??, or a precise type.

Invalid custom element name \"laberr\" i.cause: A selector that is not a valid custom element name.
Invalid custom element name \"laberr\" i.fix: Use lowercase letters and at least one dash.

Selector \"x-card\" of component \"A\" -.cause: Two components with the same selector.

Selector \"exTint\" of directive \"A\" -.cause: Two directives with the same selector.
Selector \"exTint\" of directive \"A\" -.fix: Rename one of them, ideally with a prefix.

Could not find template at <path>.cause: A templateUrl pointing to a missing file.
Could not find template at <path>.fix: Fix the path, relative to the file of the component.

The templateUrl option of XCard must be.cause: A selector, templateUrl or styleUrl given as a constant, a template literal or a computed value, or a required option missing: the plugin reads them from the source code.
The templateUrl option of XCard must be.fix: Write the value as a string literal in the decorator.

The options of @WebComponent in XCard mu.cause: The options of the decorator passed as a variable, or not passed at all.
The options of @WebComponent in XCard mu.fix: Write the options as an object literal in the decorator.

XCard must be declared in a file ending.cause: A class decorated with @WebComponent in a file that does not follow the component convention, so the plugin does not compile it.
XCard must be declared in a file ending.fix: Move the class to a file ending with .xd.component.ts.

Unsupported stylesheet extension \".styl.cause: A styleUrl that is not a .css, .scss, .sass or .less file, such as a Stylus stylesheet.

The \"sass\" package is required to comp.cause: A .scss or .sass stylesheet in a project that does not have the sass package; the same holds for a .less stylesheet without the less package. They are optional peer dependencies of @xaendar/build-tools.
The \"sass\" package is required to comp.fix: Install the package named in the message, with npm i -D sass or npm i -D less.

Failed to compile style - <path>.cause: A stylesheet the plugin could not compile: the next line gives the reason, such as an error of Sass or Less, a missing package or an unsupported extension.
Failed to compile style - <path>.fix: Fix what the next line reports, in the stylesheet at the given path or in a file it imports.

Could not find the static block applying.cause: The decorators were not compiled before the Xaendar plugin ran.
Could not find the static block applying.fix: Put the Babel plugin before xaendarPlugin().

Failed to compile component - <path>.cause: In a build, a component that cannot be compiled: its errors are printed before this message.
Failed to compile component - <path>.fix: Fix the errors printed before it.

Error: Unable to resolve module path \"..cause: An @import whose path does not resolve: a relative path leading to no file or folder, a package that is not installed, or an alias that tsconfig.json does not declare.
Error: Unable to resolve module path \"..fix: Fix the path, install the package, or declare the alias in the paths of tsconfig.json.

Module '\"<path>\"' has no exported memb.cause: An @import naming something the module does not export.
Module '\"<path>\"' has no exported memb.fix: Import it by its exact exported name; the default export is imported as default as name.

'title' is also a member of XCard: impor.cause: A name the template imports is also a member of the component, inherited ones included: an expression reading it would be ambiguous.
'title' is also a member of XCard: impor.fix: Import it under another name: @import { title as heading } from './utils.ts'.

[TypeChecker] \"root\" is reserved in te.cause: A symbol imported as root, $event or a name starting with __, which the compiler uses for itself.
[TypeChecker] \"root\" is reserved in te.fix: Import it under another name with as.

XCard does not seem to have a Render Fun.cause: The component did not compile, or the class is a subclass without its own @WebComponent.
XCard does not seem to have a Render Fun.fix: Look for the compiler message printed before it.

ReferenceError: Signal is not defined.cause: loadSignals() did not run before @xaendar/core was loaded.
ReferenceError: Signal is not defined.fix: Call it in a module loaded before the application.

Error: No directive registered for selec.cause: The template imports the directive, but its module was never loaded at runtime.
Error: No directive registered for selec.fix: Import the module in the template with @import (not @import lazy), or load it before the template is rendered.

Error: Directive TintDirective registere.cause: A custom directive applied with *, or a structural one with @@.
Error: Directive TintDirective registere.fix: Use @@ for CustomDirective and * for StructuralDirective.

Error: Selector \"exTint\" is already us.cause: Two directive classes registered with the same selector.

NotSupportedError: Failed to execute 'de.cause: Two classes defined with the same selector at runtime.

NotSupportedError: Failed to execute 'at.cause: attachShadow called by a component, which already has an open shadow root.

@import rules are not allowed here..cause: A browser warning: a component stylesheet is a constructed stylesheet, which drops the @import rules of a .css file.
@import rules are not allowed here..fix: Put every rule in the CSS file of the component, or use Sass or Less, whose imports are resolved at build time.

Circular dependency detected while compu.cause: A computed signal reading itself, directly or through others.
Circular dependency detected while compu.fix: Break the cycle with a writable signal.

Cannot set value while signals are froze.cause: A signal written, or read (Cannot get value…), inside watched, unwatched or Watcher.notify.

Cannot unwatch a signal that is not bein.cause: The disposer of an effect called when the effect is already disposed: a second time, or, for this.effect(), after the component or the directive is gone.
Cannot unwatch a signal that is not bein.fix: Call it once, while the effect is alive.

Tag <Widget> is not a valid custom eleme.cause: A component name, or a project name followed by -root, that is not a valid custom element name.
Tag <Widget> is not a valid custom eleme.fix: Use lowercase letters and a dash.

Tag <font-face> is a reserved tag name a.cause: One of the names reserved by the HTML specification.

✖ Directory \"user-card\" already exist.cause: xd generate component would overwrite an existing folder.
✖ Directory \"user-card\" already exist.fix: Pick another name, or add --force to replace it.

✖ Invalid style option: styl. Use one o.cause: A --style option of xd new that is not one of the formats the plugin compiles.
✖ Invalid style option: styl. Use one o.fix: Pass css, scss, sass or less, or leave --style out to choose the format from a list.

✖ Invalid style \"styl\" in <path>: use.cause: xd generate component found, in the nearest xaendar.json, a generate.components.style that is not one of the formats the plugin compiles.
✖ Invalid style \"styl\" in <path>: use.fix: Set it to css, scss, sass or less, or remove it to get CSS.

[Lexer] An element ref takes no value: w.cause: A value given to an element ref, as in #field="name".
[Lexer] An element ref takes no value: w.fix: Write #field alone: it names the element it is declared on.

[Lexer] An element ref names the element.cause: A #name inside the block of a conditional binding, or inside the parentheses of a directive (… outside of its directives).
[Lexer] An element ref names the element.fix: Declare the variable directly on the tag.

[Lexer] An element ref is just #name, wi.cause: Parentheses after the name of an element ref.

[Lexer] @render calls a template by its.cause: A @render without the name of the template, without parentheses, or with a space or a dot between the name and the parentheses.
[Lexer] @render calls a template by its.fix: Write @render name(arguments), with () when the template has no parameters.

[Lexer] @let declares a name and its val.cause: A @let without its name or its =, or whose block closes before its ;. The same message is reported as [Parser] when the template ends before the ;, or the value is missing.
[Lexer] @let declares a name and its val.fix: Write @let name = value; with a ; ending the value.

[Parser] <input> declares more than one.cause: Two element refs on the same element.

[Parser] <div> cannot declare #panel: it.cause: An element ref on an element a structural directive is applied to, directly or by a conditional binding.
[Parser] <div> cannot declare #panel: it.fix: Declare it on an element inside, or render the element with an @if and declare the variable inside the block.

[Parser] '2fields' is not a valid name f.cause: An element ref named by something other than an identifier; 'root' is reserved in templates is reported for root, $event and the names starting with __ or $$.
[Parser] '2fields' is not a valid name f.fix: Use an identifier the generated code does not reserve.

[Parser] '2total' is not a valid name fo.cause: A @let named by something other than an identifier; 'root' is reserved in templates is reported for root, $event and the names starting with __ or $$.
[Parser] '2total' is not a valid name fo.fix: Use an identifier the generated code does not reserve.

[Parser] A <template> declares a templat.cause: A <template> without name(…): a <template> is always the declaration of a template.
[Parser] A <template> declares a templat.fix: Name it and declare its parameters, then render it with @render.

[Parser] A <template> declares only its.cause: An attribute, an event, a conditional binding, a directive or type arguments on a <template>.
[Parser] A <template> declares only its.fix: Move them to the elements inside the template.

[Parser] The parameters of a template ar.cause: The parameters of a template with a missing or doubled comma, a semicolon, or anything but parameters.
[Parser] The parameters of a template ar.fix: Separate the parameters with single commas: name: Type, name: Type.

[Parser] The parameter 'item' of templat.cause: A parameter with neither a type nor a default value. The same message ends with cannot destructure its value, cannot be a rest parameter, cannot be both optional and with a default value, cannot have modifiers or decorators, or, for an optional parameter, needs a type.
[Parser] The parameter 'item' of templat.fix: Give each parameter a type, or a default value that gives it its type: name: Type, name = value, name: Type = value or name?: Type.

[Parser] The parameter 'index: number' o.cause: A required parameter after an optional one or one with a default value: a @render can only leave out the last arguments.
[Parser] The parameter 'index: number' o.fix: Move the required parameters first, or give this one a default value too.

[Parser] Template \"row\" declares the p.cause: Two parameters with the same name.

[Parser] '2row' cannot name a template:.cause: A @render whose name is not an identifier.
[Parser] '2row' cannot name a template:.fix: Render the template by its name.

[TypeChecker] \"field\" is read before t.cause: An interpolation, a binding, a condition, the iterable of a @for or an argument of a @render reading an element ref whose element comes after it in its scope.
[TypeChecker] \"field\" is read before t.fix: Move the element before the expression, or read the variable from an event handler, which runs once the template is rendered.

[TypeChecker] The track expression of a.cause: An element ref read by the track expression of a @for.
[TypeChecker] The track expression of a.fix: Track the item, a property of it, or $index.

Cannot redeclare block-scoped variable '.cause: Two element refs or templates with the same name in the same scope, or one named like a variable of the enclosing @for.
Cannot redeclare block-scoped variable '.fix: Rename one of them: a nested scope (a block, the row of a @for) can reuse the name.

[TypeChecker] \"row\" is not a template.cause: A @render of a name that is not a template declared in its scope or in an enclosing one: a member, an import, an element ref, or a template declared in another branch or row. The build reports it as [Generator] too.
[TypeChecker] \"row\" is not a template.fix: Declare the template where the @render can see it, or pass the data as arguments to a template declared further out.

[TypeChecker] Template \"row\" is declar.cause: A @render inside an <svg> (or a <math>) of a template declared among HTML elements, or the other way round: the content is created in the namespace of the declaration. The build reports it as [Generator] too.
[TypeChecker] Template \"row\" is declar.fix: Declare the template in the namespace of its @render.

[TypeChecker] \"field\" is read by the t.cause: The content of a template reads an element ref of an enclosing scope, outside of an event handler, and a @render of the template comes before the element of the ref.
[TypeChecker] \"field\" is read by the t.fix: Move the @render after the element, or pass the value as an argument.

[TypeChecker] \"total\" is read before i.cause: An interpolation, a binding, a condition, the iterable of a @for, an argument of a @render or the value of a @let, its own included, reading a @let that comes after it in its scope.
[TypeChecker] \"total\" is read before i.fix: Move the @let before the expression, or read it from an event handler, which runs once the template is rendered.

[TypeChecker] \"total\" is read by the t.cause: The content of a template reads a @let of an enclosing scope, outside of an event handler, and a @render of the template comes before the @let.
[TypeChecker] \"total\" is read by the t.fix: Move the @render after the @let, or pass the value as an argument.

[TypeChecker] The track expression of a.cause: A @let read by the track expression of a @for.
[TypeChecker] The track expression of a.fix: Track the item, a property of it, or $index.

Property 'toFixed' does not exist on typ.cause: A @let whose value reads a signal is a signal, read here without parentheses.

Expected 2 arguments, but got 1..cause: A @render passing fewer or more arguments than the template declares parameters: reported on the @render, or on the extra arguments.

ReferenceError: Element ref \"field\" is.cause: An event handler run while the template is still being rendered, for an event a child component emits from its onInit, reading an element ref whose element is not created yet.
ReferenceError: Element ref \"field\" is.fix: Emit the event after the render (afterRender), or read the variable later.

ReferenceError: @let \"total\" is read b.cause: An event handler run while the template is still being rendered, for an event a child component emits from its onInit, reading a @let the render has not reached yet.
ReferenceError: @let \"total\" is read b.fix: Emit the event after the render (afterRender), or read the @let later.

[Parser] The track expression of a @for.cause: A track expression that is the item or an implicit variable without parentheses: the key would be the signal, a new function every time, and no row would be reused.
[Parser] The track expression of a @for.fix: Call the signal: track item(), or track a property of it, as in track item().id.

Error: No element matches the required q.cause: A @Query.required was read while no element of the shadow root matched it: before the render (in onInit, in an effect created there, in the template), or while the element was not in the template.
Error: No element matches the required q.fix: Read it from afterRender on, in event handlers or in a computed signal read from them. If the element is not always there, use @Query.

Error: No element matches the required c.cause: A @Query.content.required was read while no projected element matched it: before the parent projected its content, afterRender included, or while the element was not projected.
Error: No element matches the required c.fix: Read it in event handlers. If the content is optional, or to follow it as it arrives, use @Query.content.

Error: @HostProperty('class.') names no.cause: A @HostProperty with class. and no class after it. Thrown when the class is defined, as soon as its module is imported; an empty name throws @HostProperty('') names no attribute.
Error: @HostProperty('class.') names no.fix: Name the attribute, or the class after class.: @HostProperty('class.on').

Error: @HostEvent() names no event.cause: A @HostEvent with an empty name. Thrown when the class is defined.

Error: @HostProperty('role') cannot deco.cause: A @HostProperty on a static field, getter or accessor: the host element belongs to an instance.
Error: @HostProperty('role') cannot deco.fix: Decorate an instance member, which may read the static one.

Error: @HostEvent('click') cannot decora.cause: A @HostEvent on a static method: the host element belongs to an instance.
